Connect $CF$ and extend it to intersect the extension of $BE$ at point $P$. If $AB=5$ and $AE=1$, what is the measure of $\angle P$? What is the length of $PC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let a perpendicular be drawn from B to CP at foot N, and from C to BP at foot M, thus CM$\perp$BP.\\
$\because$ $\triangle ABE$ is folded along line BE to obtain $\triangle FBE$,\\
$\therefore$ $Rt\triangle ABE\cong Rt\triangle FEB$,\\
$\therefore$ $BF=AB=5$, $\angle ABE=\angle PBF$,\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
$\therefore$ $BC=5$,\\
$\therefore$ $BC=BF$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BFC$ is an isosceles triangle,\\
Also, $\because$ $BN\perp FC$,\\
$\therefore$ $BN$ bisects $\angle FBC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle PBN=\angle PBF+\angle FBN=\frac{1}{2}\left(\angle ABF+\angle FBC\right)=45^\circ$,\\
In $Rt\triangle BPN$, $\angle PBN=45^\circ$, $\angle BNP=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle P=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle CMP$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $CM=MP$,\\
$\because$ $\angle ABP+\angle PBC=90^\circ$, $\angle PBC+\angle MCB=90^\circ$, $\therefore$ $\angle ABP=\angle MCB$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle EAB\sim \triangle BMC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{CM}{AB}=\frac{CB}{BE}$,\\
In $Rt\triangle ABE$, $BE=\sqrt{AB^2+AE^2}=\sqrt{26}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{CM}{5}=\frac{5}{\sqrt{26}}$, $CM=\frac{25}{\sqrt{26}}$,\\
$\therefore$ In $Rt\triangle CMP$, $PM=CM=\frac{25}{\sqrt{26}}$,\\
$\therefore$ $CP=\sqrt{CM^2+PM^2}=\boxed{\frac{25\sqrt{13}}{13}}$.

Connect $CF$ and extend it to intersect the extension of $BE$ at point $P$. If $AB=5$ and $AE=1$, what is the measure of $\angle P$? What is the length of $PC$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Let a perpendicular be drawn from B to CP at foot N, and from C to BP at foot M, thus CM$\perp$BP.\\
$\because$ $\triangle ABE$ is folded along line BE to obtain $\triangle FBE$,\\
$\therefore$ $Rt\triangle ABE\cong Rt\triangle FEB$,\\
$\therefore$ $BF=AB=5$, $\angle ABE=\angle PBF$,\\
$\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\
$\therefore$ $BC=5$,\\
$\therefore$ $BC=BF$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BFC$ is an isosceles triangle,\\
Also, $\because$ $BN\perp FC$,\\
$\therefore$ $BN$ bisects $\angle FBC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle PBN=\angle PBF+\angle FBN=\frac{1}{2}\left(\angle ABF+\angle FBC\right)=45^\circ$,\\
In $Rt\triangle BPN$, $\angle PBN=45^\circ$, $\angle BNP=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle P=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle CMP$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $CM=MP$,\\
$\because$ $\angle ABP+\angle PBC=90^\circ$, $\angle PBC+\angle MCB=90^\circ$, $\therefore$ $\angle ABP=\angle MCB$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle EAB\sim \triangle BMC$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{CM}{AB}=\frac{CB}{BE}$,\\

$\therefore$ $\frac{CM}{5}=\frac{5}{\sqrt{26}}$, $CM=\frac{25}{\sqrt{26}}$,\\
$\therefore$ In $Rt\triangle CMP$, $PM=CM=\frac{25}{\sqrt{26}}$,\\
$\therefore$ $CP=\sqrt{CM^2+PM^2}=\boxed{\frac{25\sqrt{13}}{13}}$

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Let a perpendicular be drawn from B to CP at foot N, and from C to BP at foot M, thus CM$\perp$BP.\\ $\because$ $\triangle ABE$ is folded along line BE to obtain $\triangle FBE$,\\ $\therefore$ $Rt\triangle ABE\cong Rt\triangle FEB$,\\ $\therefore$ $BF=AB=5$, $\angle ABE=\angle PBF$,\\ $\because$ Quadrilateral ABCD is a square,\\ $\therefore$ $BC=5$,\\ $\therefore$ $BC=BF$,\\ $\therefore$ $\triangle BFC$ is an isosceles triangle,\\ Also, $\because$ $BN\perp FC$,\\ $\therefore$ $BN$ bisects $\angle FBC$,\\ $\therefore$ $\angle PBN=\angle PBF+\angle FBN=\frac{1}{2}\left(\angle ABF+\angle FBC\right)=45^\circ$,\\ In $Rt\triangle BPN$, $\angle PBN=45^\circ$, $\angle BNP=90^\circ$,\\ $\therefore$ $\angle P=45^\circ$,\\ $\therefore$ $\triangle CMP$ is an isosceles right triangle,\\ $\therefore$ $CM=MP$,\\ $\because$ $\angle ABP+\angle PBC=90^\circ$, $\angle PBC+\angle MCB=90^\circ$, $\therefore$ $\angle ABP=\angle MCB$,\\ $\therefore$ $\triangle EAB\sim \triangle BMC$,\\ $\therefore$ $\frac{CM}{AB}=\frac{CB}{BE}$,\\ In $Rt\triangle ABE$, $BE=\sqrt{AB^2+AE^2}=\sqrt{26}$,\\ $\therefore$ $\frac{CM}{5}=\frac{5}{\sqrt{26}}$, $CM=\frac{25}{\sqrt{26}}$,\\ $\therefore$ In $Rt\triangle CMP$, $PM=CM=\frac{25}{\sqrt{26}}$,\\ $\therefore$ $CP=\sqrt{CM^2+PM^2}=\boxed{\frac{25\sqrt{13}}{13}}$

Image description: In the figure, there is a square ABCD, with A at the upper left, B at the lower left, C at the lower right, and D at the upper right. Point E is on the upper side AD and close to A. Line BE goes from B through E and continues to extend upward to point P. After folding, point A corresponds to the interior point F; the figure has BF and EF, and the extension from C through F also reaches P, so P is the intersection point of the extension line of BE and the extension line of CF.

Solve according to the specified coordinate method: Let A=(0,5), B=(0,0), C=(5,0), D=(5,5). Since AE=1 and E is on AD, E=(1,5). When folding triangle ABE, crease BE remains fixed, and the symmetric point of A with respect to line BE is F.

Line BE passes through B=(0,0) and E=(1,5), and its direction vector is v=(1,5). The projection of A=(0,5) in the BE direction is proj_BE(A)=((A·v)/(v·v))v=(25/26)(1,5)=(25/26,125/26). Therefore F=2proj_BE(A)-A=(25/13,60/13).

Line CP passes through C=(5,0) and F=(25/13,60/13), and its slope is (60/13-0)/(25/13-5)=(60/13)/(-40/13)=-3/2. Line BP is BE, and its equation is y=5x. The equation of line CP is y=-(3/2)(x-5). Combining y=5x and y=-(3/2)(x-5), get 5x=-(3/2)x+15/2, so x=15/13, y=75/13, namely P=(15/13,75/13).

Angle P is the angle between lines BP and CP. The slopes of the two lines are respectively m_BP=5, m_CP=-3/2, so tan θ=|(5-(-3/2))/(1+5·(-3/2))|=|(13/2)/(-13/2)|=1, therefore θ=45°.

Finally calculate PC: P=(15/13,75/13), C=(65/13,0), so PC=sqrt((65/13-15/13)^2+(0-75/13)^2)=sqrt((50/13)^2+(75/13)^2)=sqrt(8125)/13=25√13/13.
